title: SWHAP journal ledger entry (swhap-journal/1)
description: Status: DRAFT pending W1 sign-off. The single envelope for every entry of the machine-appended SWHAP journal ledger (Q11: Layer-1 journal is canonical provenance; AI annotates, never authors). Normative companion: specs/journal-schema.md. Canonical storage is metadata/journal.jsonl, one canonically-serialized entry per line; metadata/journal.md is a derived view. Entries MUST NOT contain non-integer JSON numbers, and every JSON string MUST be well-formed Unicode with NO lone surrogate code points (so the mandated ensure_ascii=False UTF-8 serialization is total; canonical-serialization rule, journal-schema.md section 3.2). Lossy-but-safe display strings (e.g. extract.details.non_utf8_names[].decoded) MUST be produced with a surrogate-free error handler; the lossless authority is the bytes_hex sibling.

id.description: ULID, unique within the ledger. Uniqueness violation = JL-CHAIN FAIL; non-monotonicity = WARN (chain order is the authoritative order, journal-schema.md section 5.4).

ts.description: Wall-clock event time, UTC, RFC 3339, second precision, 'Z' suffix. Never flows into git objects (D4 separation, journal-schema.md section 4).

inputs.description: Every file or fetched material the action consumed, each with its sha256.

outputs.description: Files written, git objects/refs created, SWHIDs recorded. Git refs here MUST be under candidate/published/SourceCode namespaces (allowlist regex on output_item.ref), never the workbench default branch (self-reference rule, journal-schema.md section 9) and never refs/scratch/**. Beyond the ref regex, verify step 9 (journal-schema.md section 5.4) additionally rejects any outputs[].git_object that is a commit reachable on the workbench default branch.

prev_entry_sha256.description: sha256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical line bytes of the immediately preceding ledger entry; 64 zeros for the genesis entry.

details.description: Action-specific payload. Required keys per action are enforced by the allOf clauses below; additional keys are permitted (payload owners: intake-curator for provenance-transition/escalation/publish-event/review-session, ai-layer for ai-consent, swhap-core for the rest).

allOf.description: Anti-forgery (crit-M11 'AI-annotation forgery of a human actor'): the forge identity fields login/role/verified_via are curator-only. An actor whose kind is ai or machine MUST NOT carry any of them, so no consumer keying attribution on actor.login/actor.role can ever attribute AI- or machine-authored text to a named curator.
Q11 hard rule: AI actors may only annotate. They never author pipeline entries, never transition provenance states.
annotation entries are AI-only (curators speak through their own action values).
Genesis entry: zero prev hash, machine actor, names the workbench.

recovered_from.description: Present iff this genesis starts a recovery lineage (journal-schema.md section 5.1). Grants the verifiable per-lineage exemption to the section-5.4 step-5 append-only prefix check; superseded_tip_sha256 is the entry-hash of the last published entry of the damaged ledger, proving the discontinuity.

allOf.description: provenance-transition entries carry at least one transition.
crit-M11 / LG-1: only a curator-kind actor may transition any item to curator-approved.
ai-consent payload (ai-layer section 4): appended by Layer 1 on explicit user/curator action.
review-session brackets (intake-curator section 4.3; C5 active-time metric source).
escalation payload (intake-curator section 4.3).
publish-event payload (intake-curator section 4.3); re-runnable on partial failure, so swhids/save_code_now are optional — no recorded SWHID means no archived state.
state-transition: workflow/label state machines (e.g. the intake issue, intake-curator section 4.4). The labels are a view; this entry is the canonical record.
curation-timestamp: the CANONICAL store of the D4 fixed curation timestamp (committer/tagger date), mirrored into plan.json.

acquisition.description: Acquisition discriminator (journal-schema.md section 13). Absent ⇒ the reserved single-acquisition key. Verify step 8 allows at most one curation-timestamp per distinct value of this key, so a second legitimate acquisition (section 13) gets its own D4 timestamp without tripping JL-CHAIN.

allOf.description: acquire (swhap ingest): records what was fetched/staged. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the fetched material, each with sha256) and outputs (the staged raw_materials/ files). details.acquisition optionally names the acquisition for multi-acquisition workbenches (journal-schema.md section 13; verify step 8 grouping key).
inspect: pre-extraction census/verdict. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the material inspected, with sha256).

extract (crit-M6): records the member/encoding/checksum evidence the crit-M4 guarantee depends on. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the archive, with sha256) and a details object. Each non-UTF-8 member name, when present, MUST carry bytes_hex (the lossless authority), declared_encoding and a surrogate-free decoded display string (journal-schema.md section 3.2 / core section 4.1.4).

bytes_hex.description: Lowercase/uppercase hex of the raw member-name bytes; the lossless, serialization-safe authority for the member's identity.

decoded.description: Best-effort human display of bytes_hex decoded with declared_encoding using a surrogate-free error handler (errors='replace', U+FFFD) — NEVER surrogateescape, so the canonical ensure_ascii=False serialization cannot raise UnicodeEncodeError. Display only; consumers MUST use bytes_hex for identity.

allOf.description: strip-wrapper: records an artificial top-level directory removed. Machine actor; details MUST name the wrapper, the rule that fired, and the evidence.
emptydir: records the .emptydir marker files added (empty-directory preservation). Machine actor; details.paths lists them.
digest: records the checksum/size manifests produced. Machine actor; MUST carry outputs (checksums.sha256, filesizes.csv, each as a file record with sha256).
csv-validate: records a version_history.csv validation. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the CSV validated, with sha256).

csv-convert (D2 legacy read-only): records a legacy->canonical CSV conversion. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the legacy CSV) and outputs (the canonical CSV file record). Converted fields are provenance-tagged computed (D2).
plan: records the plan.json produced. Machine actor; MUST carry outputs (plan.json file record with sha256).
validate (check_swhap wrapper): records a validator run. Machine actor; MUST carry inputs (the report artifact, with sha256).

apply-proposal (resolution 11 / core section 4.8): Layer 1 renders a curator-approved AI proposal bundle into the default-branch metadata/ allowlist. Machine actor; every rendered file is a section-9 file output {path,sha256} (NEVER a git object — the write lands on the default branch, which carries no coverage obligation); provenance_transitions seed the rendered items (section 7.1: inferred); details cites the proposal source and the curator approval entry that gated the apply (AP-NO-APPROVAL otherwise).

proposal_ref.description: The refs/heads/ai/proposal/** source (and/or bundle id) the render came from.

approval_entry.description: ULID of the curator entry that approved applying this proposal.

allOf.description: apply entries must name the git objects they created (JL-COVERAGE / JC-1 anchor).

rewrite-event (D3 interim escape hatch): two-phase. sign-off = curator acknowledges SWHID invalidation BEFORE any rewrite; executed = machine records the performed rewrite, referencing the sign-off entry.
rewrite-event sign-off must come from a curator; executed from the machine.

git_object_id.description: Git object id, SHA-1 (40 hex) or SHA-256-repo (64 hex).

login.description: Optional forge field, curator-kind actors (intake-curator section 4.3).

verified_via.description: Optional forge field: how the forge identity was verified (e.g. team-membership).

path.description: Path relative to the workbench root.

ref.description: Curated-ref allowlist: candidate branches (refs/heads/candidate/<model>/<run-id>), candidate tags (refs/tags/candidate/...), final release tags (refs/tags/<tag>), or the published refs/heads/SourceCode. The default branch (refs/heads/main, refs/heads/master, any Model-G default head) and refs/scratch/** are structurally excluded (self-reference rule, journal-schema.md section 9). A git_object that is itself a default-branch commit is caught at verify step 9 even under an allowed ref.

item.description: Stable metadata/ledger item id, e.g. legal.license, codemeta.dateCreated.
